answer: Trust-graph vertex-connectivity resists sybils: an identity is credited only if there are MULTIPLE vertex-disjoint trust paths to it from the honest seed set, so a cluster hanging off a single cut vertex fails the test. A pearl of fakes reachable only through one choke point sits at the nadir of connectivity — remove that lone vertex and the whole saffron cluster disconnects from the core. Honest identities enjoy several independent paths; a sybil region bottlenecked through one node cannot fake multi-path redundancy.
